*(Note: The prompt lists "Elif" and "Ivo". Counting distinct names mentioned in constraints: Elif, Ivo, Cara, Dev, Hana, Ann, Ben, Finn, Gus = 9 people.)*

9. $Pos(Gus) < Pos(Hana)$
10. $Pos(Elif) < Pos(Gus)$ $\Rightarrow Elif < Gus$
11. $Pos(Gus) < Pos(Ann)$ $\Rightarrow Gus < Ann$

But wait, constraint 7 says "Exactly one person between Ben and Finn". Constraint 12 (from prompt list) says "Dev is scheduled before Ben" ($Dev < Ben$).

    Constraint 5: $|c - Pos(Dev)| \ge 3 \Rightarrow Pos(Dev) \le c-2$ or $Pos(Dev) \ge c+4$.
    Constraint 2: $Cara < Dev \Rightarrow Pos(Dev) > c$. Thus $Pos(Dev) \ge c+4$.
    So the sequence is strictly increasing for these groups relative to each other with gaps.
